newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse edges higher on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse edges higher on foreign demand.

text.p: Increased foreign demand amid scarce supply pushed up prices on selected key shares at the Nairobi Stock Exchange, brokers and bourse officials said.

The NSE-20 share index edged up 19.21 points to close at 3447.04. Turnover was posted at 19.087 million shillngs traded on 402,441 shares compared to 17.8 million shillings on 719,949 shares on Monday.
"There is tremendous support for Kenya Commercial Bank and Kenya Power & Lighting, solid companies and potentially profitable," a senior broker said.
Foreign investors bought Kenya Commercial Bank at 105 from 102, Kenya Power at 171 from 165 and Sasini Tea & Coffee at 79 from 78.
"A number of the foreign investors are not as pessimistic as the locals are," another broker said. "In fact, a prudent person can snap up a few good shares at this time," he added.
Kakuzi eased to 105 from 108 while Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 9 from 9.05.
Kenya Airways traded at a reserve price of 8.50 on the three-day special board.
Nation Printers & Publishers eased to 115 from 120 while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 40 from 40.25.
